# This Memorial Day weekend, Easy Self Storage is honored to recognize two local heroes who made the ultimate sacrifice for our country: brothers John and George Llewellyn. 

## While the brothers grew up in neighboring Chattanooga, John has ties to the Rossville community working at the Peerless Woolen Mills. During early onset of World War II, he enlisted in the Army and was captured shortly after the attack on Pearl Harbor. Tragically, he died as a prisoner of war in the Philippines at just 27 years old. John is laid to rest in our hometown, at the Tennessee-Georgia Memorial Park in Rossville, GA. 

His brother, George Llewellyn of Chattanooga, also gave his life for his country. Serving in the Navy, George was part of the pivotal D-Day invasion where he, too, made the ultimate sacrifice. He to this day is laid to rest on the historic beaches of Normandy at the Normandy American Cemetery in France.

L55: This series contains discs representing over fifty years of recorded Irish music from the early years of the format to its obsolescence in the 1950s. Series I is also rich in examples of the Irish art song tradition featuring a wealth of recordings by Irish tenors such as Charles Harrison and John McCormack, as well as their British counterparts Father Sydney MacEwan and Michael Duffy. L56: While major labels, Columbia, Victor and Decca dominate the series, Bluebird, Brunswick, Okeh and Vocalion releases are also numerous, as are discs from smaller independent labels, particularly the small ethnic labels, Copley and Celtic. # This Memorial Day weekend, Easy Self Storage is honored to recognize two local heroes who made the ultimate sacrifice for our country: brothers John and George Llewellyn. 

## While the brothers grew up in neighboring Chattanooga, John has ties to the Rossville community working at the Peerless Woolen Mills. During early onset of World War II, he enlisted in the Army and was captured shortly after the attack on Pearl Harbor. Tragically, he died as a prisoner of war in the Philippines at just 27 years old. John is laid to rest in our hometown, at the Tennessee-Georgia Memorial Park in Rossville, GA. 

His brother, George Llewellyn of Chattanooga, also gave his life for his country. Serving in the Navy, George was part of the pivotal D-Day invasion where he, too, made the ultimate sacrifice. He to this day is laid to rest on the historic beaches of Normandy at the Normandy American Cemetery in France.
